goal_checks.notes: PresenceProvider owns the one usePresence call and exposes peers, the leader flag, publishCursor and subscribe; the rail reads the contextual value rather than calling usePresence itself. presence-provider.test.tsx proves the single call and the value; the context hook throws outside a provider.

PresenceLayer subscribes to the cursor store and paints through the peer-cursors leaf's registered paint (ref only). Cursors are denormalized with the page's displayed size/rotation (RULE-17) and filtered to the visible page; unmount unsubscribes and clears. use-presence-layer.test.ts proves the paint, the page filter and the cleanup; no React state holds a cursor.

PageStage forwards the pointer's pixel offset and the Stage size; the app normalizes through normalizePoint with the page's rotation and calls publishCursor, which throttles to ~20 Hz and only on movement (RULE-20). use-presence.test.ts pins the throttle and the wire payload (page-relative 0-1 with the page).
Provider, layer, rail and publish tests exist and pass (26 tests across the touched files), and the existing 015/028 suites still pass with the extended signatures.

cross_check_against_plan.result: matches — frontend (secondary supabase); the four mini-goals map to g1-g4; it closes 015 g2 and blocks nothing.
matches — cursors are ephemeral, ~20 Hz, ref-driven; the wire is page-relative 0-1; one client-sent topic (live:) carries them (WS/user untouched).
matches — the peer-cursors leaf is now painted and fed; the live frame-budget measurement remains 015's follow-up.

issues_found: The live two-browser Gate (latency ~100-300 ms) needs the local stack; the publish/paint path is unit-proven.
Presence tracking uses page 0 because the provider is view-level; per-page presence (which page a peer is on) is a follow-up.

The layer subscribes and repaints on every incoming cursor; a burst of peers is fine at pilot scale, but a large room would want a single rAF-coalesced repaint (the leaf's batchDraw already coalesces the draw).
The pointer publish fires on every page-stage pointermove; the throttle caps the sends, but the handler still runs per move (cheap).
